questions.question: What happens to TypeScript type annotations when your program runs?
options: They are checked again at runtime by the JavaScript engine
They are erased; only plain JavaScript executes
They are converted into runtime validation code
They make the program run faster
questions.explanation: Types exist only at compile time. tsc (or type stripping) removes them, and the JavaScript that runs has no knowledge of them.

questions.question: Which command type-checks a project without writing any JavaScript files, as CI pipelines commonly do?
questions.explanation: --noEmit runs the full type check but produces no output files. --init creates tsconfig.json and --watch re-checks on every save.

questions.question: You run `node app.ts` on Node 24 and the file contains a type error (but only erasable syntax). What happens?
options: The program runs, because Node only strips types and does not type-check
Node refuses to run the file and prints the type error
Node silently runs tsc on the file first
Node prints a warning and fixes the type automatically
questions.explanation: Node's type stripping deletes erasable annotations without checking them. You still need tsc --noEmit or your editor to find type errors.

questions.question: Which piece of TypeScript syntax cannot be run directly by Node's type stripping?
questions.explanation: Enums generate real JavaScript objects, so they cannot simply be erased. Annotations and type aliases are erasable and work with type stripping.
